title: A client-send Retry waits for its own submission and create receipt before judging previous failures
steps: Finish an accepted client-send action, then accept an explicit Retry on its existing site and chat.
Leave failed QA with eight checks on the shared build; run the scheduler before prepare and again before the browser submits the new brief.
Submit the Retry and inspect its QA, baseline and native request reservation.
Leave a failed provision receipt owned by the previous action and poll before the new provision.start; then record a failed create receipt for the new action and poll again.
expect: The newly accepted action stays queued in both scheduler windows; no server prompt or duplicate site is created.
The new request keeps the untouched baseline, resets attempts and human acceptance, and carries no previous check job or verdict.
The prior action's failed provision cannot close the new submitted Retry; a failed create receipt for this action still closes it.
evidence: Local round 41 on 27 October 2026: a newly accepted Retry failed QA_NEEDS_REVIEW before its browser submitted the brief; the old build still held failed QA with eight attempts. PostgreSQL regression reproduces failed instead of queued before the fix.
fence: reconcile requires this action's native submission before reading shared-build QA; send resets turn-owned QA atomically

tests: client-send reserves real chat and one native user request before provision; agent tools own install/check and server prompt stays zero
